items.text:
## Required executable behavior

The shared assertions use these expression names:

- `In Screening Population`
- `Completed Three Question Screen`
- `At Increased Fall Risk`
- `Exercise Intervention Applicable`
- `Consider Multifactorial Intervention`
- `Initial Population`
- `Denominator`
- `Numerator`

The first five expressions describe patient-level assessment and guidance. The
last three describe a track-authored screening-completion process measure.
Incomplete or absent screening data produces an unknown increased-risk result,
while the measure numerator remains false.

Follow the shared [participant and interoperability requirements](../../README.md),
items.rationale: Names and measure semantics are contract requirements represented by CRL Criterion exports and a manual Measure companion; Criterion declarations are not indexed as linkable leaves by this scaffold. Emitted and native expression evidence is maintained by the lead. This source acknowledgement does not attest that companion or named-expression execution has passed.

items.text:

### Excluded - diagnosis or emergency triage after a fall - automatic ordering of an intervention - inpatient, hospice, or long-term-care populations - equivalence claims to CMS139FHIR - real-world quality reporting or clinical deployment

## Coded Questionnaire contract

| linkId | LOINC 2.81 | Display | Answer type |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `unsteady` | `100257-5` | Feel unsteady when standing or walking | Boolean |
| `worries-about-falling` | `97878-3` | Worried about falling | Boolean |
| `fallen-in-past-year` | `52552-7` | Falls in the past year | Boolean |

The codes were resolved and verified as active through ReasonHub on
2026-08-26. The track does not assign a panel code because these three items
are a deliberate subset rather than a claim to implement the complete LOINC
Stay Independent panel.
items.rationale: The three source LOINC 2.81 question codes are declared in CRL terminology. Their binding on generated question/extracted Observation output remains a separate unmet contract; local answer codes are not represented as those LOINC codes.

items.text:
FHIR R4 `QuestionnaireResponse.item` has no `code` element. Each response
therefore retains Boolean answers and references the versioned shared
Questionnaire, where the LOINC codes are maintained. SDC extraction repeats
those codes on the resulting `Observation.code`. This preserves conformant
FHIR and straightforward Boolean logic in CQL.
items.rationale: Source explains Questionnaire versus QuestionnaireResponse code placement and expected extraction. Actual generated shared-QR/extraction interoperability has not been established; no clinical decision link can substitute for it.

items.text: A response is complete only when its status is `completed` and all three
items.rationale: OPEN: original QuestionnaireResponse.status=completed is required by source. The model uses three local selected answer records and cannot establish original shared-response status/association. This source requirement deliberately has no linked implementation.

items.text:
items contain a usable Boolean answer. Increased fall risk is true when the
response is complete and at least one answer is true. It is false when the
response is complete and all answers are false. It is null when the response is
incomplete or absent.
items.rationale: The local-answer portion is implemented by presence predicates and nullable risk logic. Combined with the separately open completed-QR-status item, this does not claim that all original shared-response semantics are satisfied.

items.text:
## SDC extraction contract

The shared Questionnaire declares the SDC
[`sdc-questionnaire-extr-obsn`](https://hl7.org/fhir/uv/sdc/STU4/en/StructureDefinition-sdc-questionnaire-extr-obsn.html)
profile, enables `sdc-questionnaire-observationExtract`, and supplies the
`survey` Observation category. The four completed responses are expected to
produce three final Observations. Each Observation copies the patient,
encounter, authored time, author, coded question, and Boolean answer, and its
`derivedFrom` points to the source QuestionnaireResponse.
items.rationale: OPEN: SDC profile/enablement and exact final Observation fields, including encounter, authored time, author, question coding and derivedFrom, require their own producer checks. A CRL-generated local answer record is not claimed to satisfy this contract.

items.text:
SDC [`QuestionnaireResponse/$extract`](https://hl7.org/fhir/uv/sdc/STU4/en/OperationDefinition-QuestionnaireResponse-extract.html)
can return a transaction Bundle. To make cross-implementation comparisons
stable, each `extracted-bundle.json` is instead a collection Bundle containing
only the normalized expected resource set. Its deterministic `fullUrl` values
identify fixture resources and are not part of the semantic assertion; the
track does not prescribe server-local URLs, request verbs, or
conditional-create behavior.
items.rationale: Fixture collection Bundle format is the normalized expected set; server URLs and transaction verbs are not semantic requirements. No requirement for two servers owned by this participant is inferred.

items.text:
The incomplete response and absent-response cases intentionally have an empty
expected resource set and `invocationExpected=false`. The track does not invoke
the baseline extraction operation until a completed QuestionnaireResponse is
available, so a partial affirmative answer cannot leak into downstream logic
as if the assessment were complete.
items.rationale: OPEN: the decision guards prevent incomplete local answer sets producing guidance, but do not implement the separate SDC invocationExpected=false rule for partial/absent shared QuestionnaireResponses. No linked extraction implementation is claimed.

items.text:
## Assertion format

Every assertion has an expression name and an expected typed value. Boolean
unknown is represented as JSON `null` with `"semantics": "unknown"`; it is
not interchangeable with `false`, an omitted result, or an execution error.

A test harness may add raw engine output and status fields in a separate result
file. It should not modify the shared assertions.
items.rationale: Preserve original typed assertions. Null is distinct from false, absence and engine error. This defines verification, not a substitute decision or a claim that the native run passed.

items.text:
## Fixture validation status

On 2026-08-26, all 13 FHIR files passed the HL7 FHIR validator 6.10.2 with
FHIR R4 4.0.1 and `hl7.fhir.uv.sdc#4.0.0` with no errors. Remaining warnings
are limited to omitted generated narratives, the deliberately missing required
answer in the incomplete fixture, and LOINC validation being disabled in that
validator run. Exact ReasonHub lookups independently confirmed all three LOINC
2.81 codes and displays as active. Cross-file checks also confirmed that every
completed answer is reproduced exactly in the expected Observation and that
the original eight CQL assertions remain unchanged.
items.rationale: Historical validation status of supplied fixtures; not validation or clinical approval of this generated artifact.

# Older-adult fall risk (STEADI)

This case supplies a traceable source corpus, synthetic FHIR R4 patient
bundles, a shared coded Questionnaire, and engine-neutral expected results.
Participants turn the source material into evidence, assessment, guidance,
and screening-completion measure artifacts.

## Clinical question
items.rationale: Source identity, supplied-file heading and challenge introduction; these identify the corpus and authoring purpose, not additional clinical eligibility criteria.

items.text:
1. Is the patient in scope for fall-risk screening?
2. Was the CDC STEADI three-question screen completed?
3. Does the completed screen indicate increased fall risk?
4. Which evidence-linked action is applicable?
5. Across a measurement period, what proportion of eligible patients completed
   the screen?
items.rationale: The five use-case questions organize assessment, guidance and the completion measure. Their detailed executable requirements are attributed separately; this item does not assert that measure execution or every output is complete.

## Case contents

- [Source manifest](sources/manifest.yaml) and [raw source snapshots](sources/raw/)
- [MARP overview](slides/connectathon-track-overview.md) and
  [rendered PDF](slides/connectathon-track-overview.pdf)
- [Synthetic patient test bundles](test-bundles/README.md), a shared coded
  [Questionnaire](test-bundles/questionnaire.json), SDC extraction
  expectations, assertions, and a case summary for every bundle

The raw corpus contains only snapshots whose current redistribution basis is
recorded in the manifest. Standards references and CMS139FHIR remain link-only.
CMS139FHIR is a comparison point; it is not copied, and the track-authored
measure must not claim equivalence to it.

## Participant deliverables

The expected output includes:

| Knowledge role | Expected artifact |
| --- | --- |
| Evidence and population definitions | `Evidence`, `EvidenceVariable` |
| Three-question assessment | `Questionnaire`, reusable logic |
| Recommendation workflow | `PlanDefinition`, `ActivityDefinition`, `Library` |
| Screening-completion measure | `Measure`, `Library` |
| Terminology and package metadata | `ValueSet`, `ImplementationGuide` |
| Executable logic | CQL source and ELM JSON |
| Distribution | FHIR R4 NPM package with exact dependency versions |

FHIR R4 does not define `Citation`; an R4 baseline submission should use
available provenance and related-artifact elements. Any R5 variant must be
clearly separated from the R4 baseline.

## SDC extraction contract

The input fixtures exercise the SDC Observation-based extraction pattern.
Each completed QuestionnaireResponse references the same versioned,
LOINC-coded Questionnaire. Its expected extracted Observations are supplied as
a normalized resource set so participants can compare `$extract` behavior
across implementations without depending on server-specific transaction
details. Incomplete and absent responses remain explicit negative extraction
cases.

The [fixture contract](test-bundles/README.md#sdc-extraction-contract) defines
the coded questions, copied Observation fields, extraction invocation rules,
and Boolean/null semantics.

Proposed HL7 FHIR Connectathon 43 track
# AI-Assisted Development of Clinical Reasoning Knowledge

Testing how clinical source material can become valid, clinically coherent, interoperable FHIR and CQL knowledge artifacts.

September 19–20, 2026 · Rockville, Maryland

---
Purpose and intent
## The track evaluates AI-assisted authoring of computable clinical knowledge
### Hypothesis AI-assisted methods can reduce the time and human effort needed to develop computable clinical knowledge, and can support more artifact types with a repeatable process.
### Required result The resulting knowledge must remain source-traceable, structurally valid, clinically coherent, executable, and portable across independent implementations.
---
Evaluation questions
## The track records process performance and artifact quality | Dimension | What the track records | | --- | --- | | **Efficiency** | elapsed authoring time, human review time, revision cycles, and blocking issues | | **Scalability** | artifact types completed, reuse of the process, and response to source changes | | **Validity** | FHIR validation, canonical resolution, CQL translation, and package checks | | **Clinical coherence** | reviewer findings, corrections, internal consistency, and expected clinical behavior | | **Interoperability** | equivalent results across CQL engines and preservation across FHIR repositories |

Where a participant has a comparable conventional baseline, it should be reported. Otherwise, efficiency findings remain descriptive.

---
Common test design
## Participants use common inputs and acceptance criteria

01 · Inputs

Approved clinical source corpus and shared use-case statement.

02 · Method

Any AI-assisted or conventional authoring approach.

03 · Disclosure

Record tools, versions, instructions, decisions, and human review.

04 · Outputs

The same required knowledge artifacts and executable behaviors.

05 · Evaluation

The same validation, clinical review, fixtures, and interoperability tests.

No participant implementation defines the reference result. The documented clinical intent and expected behaviors do.

---
Use case
items.rationale: Participant verification/process requirements, synthetic-use warning, MARP presentation metadata, evaluation dimensions and authoring-method overview. These are real reporting obligations, not screening eligibility branches. Independent execution/round-trip/human review must be reported according to actual performance and operator-scoped skips.

## The baseline defines a narrow clinical scope
### Included

Source material
## The source corpus covers evidence, recommendation, workflow, and formalization | Source | Role in the use case | | --- | --- | | **CDC STEADI algorithm and pocket guide** | three-question assessment and screen–assess–intervene workflow | | **USPSTF 2024 recommendation** | exercise recommendation and individualized multifactorial consideration | | **USPSTF evidence update and open systematic review** | population, outcomes, benefits, harms, and evidence context | | **LOINC and HL7 CPG / Using CQL with FHIR** | terminology and computable-artifact guidance | | **CMS139FHIR** | comparison point only; not copied or represented as the track measure |

Source-to-output mapping
## Each source role has a defined computable destination | Source role | Structured knowledge | Primary FHIR output | | --- | --- | --- | | Evidence review | benefits, harms, population, outcomes | `Evidence`, `EvidenceVariable` | | Recommendation | applicability, strength, action | `PlanDefinition`, `ActivityDefinition`, `Library` | | STEADI workflow | screening and follow-up decisions | `PlanDefinition`, `ActivityDefinition` | | Three-question screen | questions, answers, completeness, positive result | `Questionnaire`, `Library` | | Track measure definition | population and completion logic | `Measure`, `Library` | | Terminology and packaging guidance | bindings, dependencies, canonical identity | `ValueSet`, `ImplementationGuide` | ---
Expected output
## The submission includes reviewable knowledge and FHIR R4 artifacts
### Reviewable knowledge Evidence summary · recommendation decision table · assessment definition · measure definition · terminology definition
### FHIR knowledge artifacts `Evidence` · `EvidenceVariable` · `Questionnaire` · `Library` · `PlanDefinition` · `ActivityDefinition`
### Measure and package `Measure` · `ValueSet` · `ImplementationGuide` · stable canonicals · exact dependency versions
Every clinical statement and operational choice must be distinguishable and traceable to its source or track-authored rationale.

Expected executable behavior
items.rationale: Slide source-role and output-family mapping, evidence context, source links and packaging requirements. This does not import the linked clinical documents or assert that companion/native/package work has passed. The lead must report actual artifact and interoperability evidence.

items.text:
## CQL expresses assessment, guidance, and measure semantics
### Required named behaviors - `In Screening Population` - `Completed Three Question Screen` - `At Increased Fall Risk` - `Exercise Intervention Applicable` - `Consider Multifactorial Intervention` - `Initial Population`, `Denominator`, `Numerator`
### Deliverable package - CQL source using a portable subset - translated ELM JSON and translation logs - FHIR R4 NPM package - synthetic patient Bundles - engine-neutral expected results - exact translator, engine, and dependency versions
---
Clinical coherence
items.rationale: Duplicate named assessment/measure exports and executable package contract. Source acknowledgement identifies these required outputs; it is not a claim of native proof or of direct CRL Measure/Evidence support.

items.text:
## Human review verifies that the artifacts tell the same clinical story
### Review questions - Are source statements separated from track-authored choices? - Are population, recommendation strength, and actions preserved? - Do the assessment, guideline, measure, and CQL agree? - Are uncertainty and incomplete data represented explicitly?
### Failure examples - missing answer treated as a negative answer - increased risk represented as a diagnosis - exercise and multifactorial recommendations collapsed - unsupported code, threshold, or population invented - measure represented as CMS139FHIR
FHIR validation and CQL compilation are necessary, but they are not clinical approval.
---
items.rationale: Review questions, failure examples and clinical-approval limitation guide verification. They do not introduce another patient-level decision. Missing/unknown and separate guidance are attributed in the clinical items; validation is not clinical approval.

items.text:
Shared test cases
## Synthetic fixtures make the expected behavior observable | Case | Expected result | | --- | --- | | Adult younger than 65 | outside screening and measure population | | Eligible adult; all answers no | complete screen; not at increased risk | | Eligible adult; unsteady yes | increased risk; exercise applicable | | Eligible adult; prior fall yes | increased risk; multifactorial consideration | | Eligible adult; incomplete response | screen incomplete; risk unknown; numerator false | | Eligible adult; no response | screen incomplete; risk unknown; numerator false |
Missing data must remain unknown. It must not silently become a negative screen.
---
items.rationale: Duplicate six-case source oracle and warning against treating unknown as false. The source cases are retained independently of authoring predictions; original shared-QR and native evidence limits still apply.

items.text:
Interoperability testing
## Interoperability testing covers validation, translation, execution, and storage

01 · Validate

Validate FHIR R4 resources and the package.

02 · Round-trip

Store and retrieve artifacts from independent FHIR repositories.

03 · Translate

Translate the same CQL and record diagnostics.

04 · Execute

Run every synthetic fixture in independent CQL engines.

05 · Compare

Compare values, null semantics, versions, and discrepancies.

Baseline acceptance requires agreement across at least two independent CQL implementations and round-trip testing in at least two FHIR implementations.

---
Expected track result
## The outcome is evidence about the process and the artifacts
### Process evidence - authoring and review effort - revision history and human decisions - repeatability across knowledge-artifact types - implementation-specific limitations
### Knowledge evidence - reviewed source-to-output traceability - valid FHIR and translatable CQL - clinically coherent fixture behavior - cross-implementation result matrix and issue list

The central question: can AI-assisted development improve efficiency and scale while preserving clinical quality and interoperability?
items.rationale: Track-level validation, translation, independent execution/storage, comparison and process-evidence expectations. Operator excluded participant round-trip coordination for this demo; no such run is claimed and no new patient eligibility condition follows.
